summary: A playful, emotional webpage asking a girl named Saachi to come back. Harry Potter themed with Slytherin house aesthetic. Features a heartfelt message with the line 'you are my patronus Saachi', a 'Yes' button and a 'No' button that runs away when hovered/clicked and displays random witty quips. Saachi has a nickname 'Windshields' (due to her glasses) which is integrated. The core message is asking her to reconnect — lighter and less overwhelming than 'please come back', with a hopeful, sweet tone. The 🥺 emoji has been removed from all text across the app.
architectural_notes: 'You are my Patronus, Saachi 🥺' line must always be present on the main page — do not remove it.
Do NOT mention 'the date' or any date context in the main page message — the messaging should simply ask Saachi to please come back, nothing more.
The nickname 'Windshields' must always be paired with an affectionate qualifier (e.g. 'my fav Windshields') — never used alone in a way that could sound rude or insulting.
The main page message tone should feel light and inviting — avoid heavy 'please come back' phrasing; prefer softer language around reconnecting or a gentle invitation.
The 🥺 emoji must not appear anywhere in the app — it has been removed from all components and all text.
known_issues: 'You are my Patronus, Saachi 🥺' line was accidentally removed from the main page in a recent build.
The intelligence compliment line in MainCard feels unnatural and forced — needs to be rewritten to flow organically within the existing message.

existing_features.title: Create a main page with a heartfelt, centered message addressed to 'Saachi', asking her to please come back and give a second chance to make things right. The message must prominently feature the 🥺 emoji and be written in a sweet, sincere tone.

Add a 'Yes 🥺' button and a 'No' button below the message. When 'Yes' is clicked, display a joyful celebratory response screen with confetti animation, hearts, and a happy message like 'Yay! I promise to make it right!'. The Yes button should be large, visually prominent, and inviting.

Make the 'No' button run away whenever the user tries to hover over it or click it: the button must animate and teleport to a random position on screen within viewport bounds each time the cursor approaches or clicks it. Each time it runs away, it must also display a random witty playful quip near the button. The quips should cycle through a predefined list of at least 10 varied quips such as: 'Nope!', 'You sure about that?', 'Try again!', 'Nice try!', 'I am faster than you!', 'That is not an option!', 'You cannot click me!', 'Almost!', 'Not today!', 'Keep dreaming!'.

Apply a romantic, soft, and whimsical visual theme: use warm rose and pink and cream tones, elegant flowing typography for the main message, floating heart or petal animations in the background, and a layout that feels emotionally inviting. Ensure the design is consistent across all states including initial, yes response, and no-button-running states.
Render the generated romantic background image as a static asset from frontend/public/assets/generated and apply it as the full-page background.

Redesign the full visual theme of the app to be Harry Potter themed with a Slytherin house aesthetic. Replace the current romantic rose/pink/cream palette with Slytherin colors: deep emerald green, silver, and dark charcoal/near-black. Update typography to feel magical and wizarding (use a serif or gothic-style font for headings where possible). Replace floating hearts/petals background animations with magical elements such as floating golden sparks, stars, or magical particles. Update all UI components (MainCard, CelebrationScreen, RunawayButton, FloatingHearts) to reflect the Slytherin/Harry Potter theme consistently across all states (initial, yes-celebration, and no-button-running).

Add the line 'You are my Patronus, Saachi 🥺' somewhere prominently on the main page, integrated naturally into or below the existing heartfelt message. Style it to feel magical and emotionally resonant, consistent with the Slytherin/Harry Potter theme.

Generate a new full-page background image with a Harry Potter / Slytherin aesthetic: a dark, magical scene featuring deep emerald greens, silver accents, soft magical glowing effects (like floating lights or spell sparks), and a moody enchanted atmosphere evoking the Slytherin common room or a magical castle dungeon. Replace the existing romantic background image with this new one, applying it as the full-page background in App.tsx.

Integrate Saachi's nickname 'Windshields' (earned from her glasses) naturally into the main page message. This could appear as a playful, affectionate aside or secondary line alongside or below the primary message addressing 'Saachi', e.g. 'my Windshields' or 'Saachi (aka Windshields)'. It should feel warm and personal, consistent with the Slytherin/Harry Potter theme.

Update all messaging across the app (MainCard, CelebrationScreen, and any quips in RunawayButton) to reflect that they only went on one date — not a relationship. Remove any phrasing that implies the user 'messed up', 'made a mistake', or 'ruined something'. Reframe the tone as: 'we had one magical date and I'd love another chance to see where this goes', hopeful and light rather than apologetic or remorseful.

Update the main page message in MainCard to clearly reflect the context: she left after the first date saying 'this isn't working out', and the message is simply asking her to please come back and give it another chance. The tone must be sweet, hopeful, and sincere — centered on 'please come back 🥺' — without any framing of messing up, mistakes, or apologies. Remove any language that implies a longer relationship or wrongdoing.

Update the CelebrationScreen (shown after 'Yes' is clicked) so its messaging aligns with the one-date context — celebrating the prospect of a second date, not 'making things right' or fixing anything. It should feel joyful and forward-looking, e.g. 'Yay! Can't wait for our next date! 🥺'.
Audit and update all quips in RunawayButton to ensure none imply a relationship, wrongdoing, or apology context. All quips should remain playful and witty, consistent with the one-date scenario.

Update the main page message in MainCard to remove any mention of 'the date', 'first date', 'second date', or any date-related framing entirely. The message should simply and sincerely ask Saachi to come back, with a heartfelt, hopeful tone — no contextual framing whatsoever. Keep the 🥺 emoji prominent, retain the 'You are my Patronus, Saachi 🥺' line, and keep the 'Windshields' nickname reference. The tone should be pure 'please come back, I miss you' — sweet and direct.

Update the CelebrationScreen messaging to remove any reference to 'dates', 'a second date', or date-related framing. The celebration should simply express joy that Saachi said yes to coming back, e.g. 'Yay! You're coming back! 🥺', with no mention of a date.

Audit all quips in RunawayButton and remove any that reference dates, dating, or 'going on a date'. Replace any removed quips with new playful, witty quips that are context-free and simply tease the user for trying to click No.

Update all occurrences of the 'Windshields' nickname in MainCard (main page message) to use a cuter, more affectionate phrasing. Replace bare 'Windshields' or 'aka Windshields' with something warm and endearing such as 'my fav Windshields' or 'my favourite Windshields'. The nickname must never appear standalone or in a way that could read as insulting or rude — it should feel like a term of affection.

Update the CelebrationScreen so that any occurrence of 'Windshields' in the celebration message (e.g. 'Windshields said Yes!') is replaced with a cuter affectionate form such as 'my fav Windshields said Yes!' or 'my favourite Windshields is coming back!'. It must not sound rude or cold.

In the MainCard component (frontend/src/App.tsx), add a warm, sincere compliment about Saachi's intelligence/brain to the kind, heartfelt section of the main page message. The compliment should feel genuine and personal — e.g. something like 'I love how brilliant your mind is' or 'your intelligence is one of the things I adore most about you'. It must fit naturally into the existing message flow, maintain the Slytherin/Harry Potter magical tone, and never feel forced or out of place.

In the CelebrationScreen component (frontend/src/components/CelebrationScreen.tsx), add a warm, heartfelt line expressing that Saachi made the sender the happiest — e.g. 'You made me the happiest person in the world 🥺' or 'You just made me the happiest 🥺'. This line should appear prominently on the celebration screen after the user clicks Yes, feel emotionally sincere and joyful, and be consistent with the existing Slytherin/Harry Potter magical theme and typography.

In the MainCard component (frontend/src/App.tsx), rewrite the intelligence compliment about Saachi so it flows organically and naturally within the existing message. The current line feels forced or out of place — rework its wording and position within the message so it reads as a seamless, sincere part of the heartfelt text, not an awkward addition. The compliment should still genuinely praise her brilliance/intelligence, maintain the Slytherin/Harry Potter magical tone, and never feel tacked on.

In the MainCard component (frontend/src/App.tsx), find the intelligence compliment about Saachi and replace the word 'mind' with 'intelligence' wherever it appears in that compliment line. For example, if the line reads something like 'I love how brilliant your mind is', change it to 'I love how brilliant your intelligence is' (or equivalent natural phrasing using 'intelligence' instead of 'mind'). The line must still read naturally and flow organically within the existing message.

In the MainCard component (frontend/src/App.tsx), replace any 'please come back' phrasing in the main page message with a softer, lighter invitation — framed around reconnecting or gently reaching out rather than a heavy plea. For example, use phrasing like 'Can we reconnect? 🥺', 'I'd love to hear from you again 🥺', or 'Maybe we could start again? 🥺'. The new phrasing must still feel heartfelt and sincere, keep the 🥺 emoji prominent, retain the 'You are my Patronus, Saachi 🥺' line, keep the 'my fav Windshields' nickname reference, and remain consistent with the Slytherin/Harry Potter magical tone.

Remove every instance of the 🥺 emoji from all text in the frontend, including but not limited to: the main page message in App.tsx (MainCard), the 'You are my Patronus, Saachi' line, the Yes button label, the CelebrationScreen messages, and any quips or strings in RunawayButton. No 🥺 emoji should appear anywhere in the rendered UI.
